# Cratebase

> Cratebase is a self-hostable backend server, written in Rust: dynamic
> data collections, authentication, file storage, and realtime
> subscriptions over one REST API, backed by SQLite (default, zero config)
> or PostgreSQL (same code, same API — set `DATABASE_URL`), distributed as
> a single executable that also serves an embedded admin dashboard.

Use this file to quickly understand the project's shape before reading
source. Everything referenced below is real and current, not aspirational.

## Run it

- `docker compose up` — sqlite + local disk storage, zero config.
- `docker compose --profile postgres --profile s3 up` — + Postgres + RustFS
  (S3-compatible storage), see [.env.example](./.env.example) for every
  variable.
- From source: `cargo build --release -p cratebase-server`, then
  `cratebase serve`. A fresh instance with no superuser yet shows an
  inline setup form at `http://localhost:8090` (`GET /api/setup/status`,
  `POST /api/setup`) — no CLI required. `cratebase superuser create
  you@example.com yourpassword` still works for scripted setup. Full
  dashboard requires `bun run admin:build` first
  (see [ARCHITECTURE.md](./ARCHITECTURE.md#the-admin-dashboard-is-not-a-separate-deployment)).

## Core concepts

- **Collection** — a user-defined table with a JSON-described schema
  (fields, types, required/unique) and five API rules
  (list/view/create/update/delete). Three kinds: `base` (plain data),
  `auth` (gets `email`/`password` and the auth endpoints below for free),
  and `view` (backed by a `SELECT`, read-only).
- **Record** — one row in a collection. Every record has `id`, `created`,
  `updated`, `collectionId`, `collectionName` plus its schema fields.
- **API rule** — `null` = superusers only, `""` = public, or a filter
  expression (`owner = @request.auth.id`) evaluated per request/row.
- **Filter expression** — the same small language used for `?filter=`
  query params and API rules: `field = "value" && (a > 1 || b ~ "text")`,
  with `@request.auth.*` / `@request.data.*` context variables.

## API shape (base path `/api`)

- `GET /health`
- `GET /setup/status`, `POST /setup` — first-run superuser creation; closed
  once any superuser exists.
- `GET/POST /collections`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /collections/{idOrName}`
  (superuser only — this is schema management)
- `GET/POST /collections/{idOrName}/records`,
  `GET/PATCH/DELETE /collections/{idOrName}/records/{id}`
  (list supports `?filter=`, `?sort=`, `?page=`, `?perPage=`; create/update
  accept JSON or `multipart/form-data` when the collection has file fields)
- `POST /batch` — several record create/update/upsert/delete calls (JSON
  or multipart, for file fields) in one HTTP round trip and one SQL
  transaction.
- Auth, on `auth`-type collections (registration is just `POST
  .../records` with `password`/`passwordConfirm`; superusers are the
  built-in `_superusers` auth collection, so superuser login is `POST
  /collections/_superusers/auth-with-password`, not a separate endpoint):
  - `POST /collections/{c}/auth-with-password`, `POST /collections/{c}/auth-refresh`,
    `GET /collections/{c}/auth-methods`
  - `POST /collections/{c}/request-verification`, `POST /collections/{c}/confirm-verification`
  - `POST /collections/{c}/request-password-reset`, `POST /collections/{c}/confirm-password-reset`
  - `POST /collections/{c}/request-email-change`, `POST /collections/{c}/confirm-email-change`
  - `POST /collections/{c}/request-otp`, `POST /collections/{c}/auth-with-otp`
  - `POST /collections/{c}/impersonate/{id}` (superuser only)
- `GET /files/{collection}/{recordId}/{filename}`
- `GET /realtime` (SSE; first event carries a `clientId`),
  `POST /realtime` with `{clientId, subscriptions: ["collection", "collection/recordId"]}`
- JS hooks: a `pb_hooks/*.pb.js` file next to the data directory can add
  native-style lifecycle hooks (`onRecordCreate`, ...) and mount extra
  root-level HTTP routes via `routerAdd` — see
  [ARCHITECTURE.md](./ARCHITECTURE.md#extending-with-javascript-cratesjsvm).

Full machine-readable spec: [openapi.yaml](./openapi.yaml).
Error bodies are always `{ "code": 400, "message": "...", "data": { field: { code, message } } }`.

## Client SDK

Cratebase's API is byte-compatible with PocketBase v0.23+, so there's no
bespoke client to install: `npm install pocketbase` (or any of
PocketBase's other official SDKs) works unchanged — persisted
`authStore`, multipart file upload helpers, and realtime subscriptions
included. See the [pocketbase package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/pocketbase).

## Source map

- `crates/core` — domain types (`Collection`, `Field`), no I/O.
- `crates/filter` — the filter expression parser + SQL compiler.
- `crates/db` — the storage engine (SQLite/Postgres via sqlx `Any`,
  collection<->table sync, record CRUD, rule enforcement).
- `crates/storage` — file storage (local disk or any S3-compatible bucket).
- `crates/auth` — password hashing, JWT session/action tokens, OTP hashing.
- `crates/jsvm` — embedded QuickJS runtime backing `pb_hooks/` and `routerAdd`.
- `crates/mailer` — pluggable mail backend (Resend API, SMTP, or log-only).
- `crates/server` — the axum HTTP API, CLI, plugin system, `jsvm`/`mailer`
  wiring, and embedded admin dashboard.
- `web/admin` — the admin dashboard source (React + Vite + TanStack).

Read [ARCHITECTURE.md](./ARCHITECTURE.md) for how these fit together and
the specific, deliberate trade-offs (e.g. why booleans are stored as
integers, why realtime is single-node). Read [ROADMAP.md](./ROADMAP.md) for
what's intentionally not built yet (realtime beyond a single node, admin
audit log, per-collection rate limiting).
